nodes_changed.name: Backlog
nodes_changed.doc:
The bytes of replies one connection holds, shared by its producers and

its feed.

nodes_changed.name: offer_replies
nodes_changed.doc:
Queues reply `frames` in order without waiting, unless the replies

would pass the backlog bound.

nodes_changed.name: reply
nodes_changed.doc:
Delivers the apply loop's reply `frames`, in order, to every

connection of `session_id`, without waiting. A connection whose

queued replies would pass the bound is evicted rather than waited

on, so a stalled tab never holds up the replies to the others.

nodes_changed.name: subscribe
nodes_changed.doc:
Registers a new connection of `session_id` and returns its feed. The

connection receives every frame sent to the session from now on,

until the feed is dropped.

nodes_changed.name: a_tab_paused_past_the_grace_keeps_its_replies_while_nothing_waits_on_it
nodes_changed.doc:
A paused reader whose queue holds only replies keeps them however

long it pauses: no producer waits on it, so only the reply backlog

bound can evict it. Over Connect a paused reader stops taking frames

as soon as its HTTP/2 window fills, so a pause of the grace or more

is ordinary, and evicting it lost frames it was about to take.

nodes_changed.name: overflow_replies
nodes_changed.doc: Evicts the only tab of `s` by passing its reply backlog bound.

node.name: SessionFeed
node.doc:
One connection's view of its session's frames, in send order.



Dropping it unregisters the connection, which releases any producer

waiting on its queue.

node.name: took
node.doc:
Accounts for a frame taken off the queue and hands it over; a data

frame's slot is released as it drops here.

node.name: session_subscribe
node.doc:
Registers a connection of `session_id`; its feed receives every

session frame, losslessly, until dropped.

node.name: session_subscribe
node.doc: Registers a connection of `session_id` and returns its lossless feed.

node.name: Registration
node.doc: Unregisters a connection's sink when its feed is dropped.

node.name: recv
node.signature: pub(crate) async fn recv(&mut self) -> Result<Vec<u8>, FellBehind>
node.doc:
The next frame for this connection.



Cancel safe: a frame is taken only when this returns it.



# Errors



[`FellBehind`] once the connection has been evicted, ahead of any

frame still queued; the transport must close it so the client

reconnects and resyncs.

node.name: SessionStreams
node.doc: Per-session connection queues keyed by session id.

node.name: evict
node.doc: Removes a connection that could not keep up and tells its feed.

node.name: send
node.signature: pub(super) async fn send(&self, session_id: &str, frame: Vec<u8>)
node.doc:
Delivers a data `frame` to every connection of `session_id`, waiting

for room in each queue (a frame slot and the frame's bytes), at most

the grace per connection. Returns

once every live connection has the frame queued or has been evicted.

A session with no connections drops the frame: nobody is there to

receive it.

node.name: a_stalled_tab_does_not_hold_up_replies_to_the_sessions_other_tabs
node.doc:
A tab that stops reading does not hold up the session's command replies:

the apply loop answers the other tabs at once instead of waiting on the

stalled one's full queue.

node.name: reply_to_session
node.doc:
Delivers the apply loop's reply `frames` to every connection of

`session_id` without waiting (see [`SessionStreams::reply`]).

node.name: reply_to_session
node.doc:
Delivers the session apply loop's reply `frames` to every connection of

`session_id`, in order, without waiting on any of them. The apply loop

serves every tab of the session, so one tab's slow socket must not hold

up another's replies; a tab that cannot take them is closed instead.

node.name: run_session_actor
node.signature: pub(crate) async fn run_session_actor( session_id: String, state: AppState, mut inputs: mpsc::Receiver<SessionInput>, )
node.doc:
Runs one session's apply loop. It drains client frames from every

connection (tab) of the session in arrival order and applies each one

to completion before the next. This single consumer is the

session-level serializability guarantee — two tabs' commands can no

longer interleave mid-apply (RFD-0113). The loop ends when

the session's last connection drops and the channel closes.
